rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī recounts that Nimrod's tower, said to be five thousand cubits or two farsakhs high to reach heaven, was struck at its foundations; the wind carried off its top and the rest fell on its builders.
rows.anchor: ارتفاعه خمسة آلاف ذراع أو فرسخان ليتوصل به نمرود كما زعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian's settlement could not protect its people when the punishment arrived as an earthquake.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب مدين لما أتاهم العذاب فأخذتهم الرجفة الرجفة لما تغن عنهم مدنيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Thicket fled oppressive heat into caves, found them hotter, then gathered under the cool-breezed cloud whose fire burned them.
rows.anchor: وإن كانوا هم أصحاب الأيكة فإنهم لما اشتد عليهم الحر يوم الظلة قصدوا المغارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people were struck suddenly: their towns were overturned after being raised skyward, then fiery brimstone stones followed.
rows.anchor: وأما قوم لوط فأتاهم الأمر بغته , لم يشعروا حتى قلبت مدائنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He singles out Lot's people because Arabs passed the sites of their overturned towns and could see them.
rows.anchor: ولعله خص قوم لوط بالذكر من بين من ليس له هذا اوصف لأن العرب كانوا يمرون على مواضع مدائنهم ويشاهدونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Lot's people the overturned towns links their reversal of sexual conduct to the hypocrites' reversal of truth; hypocrites deserve comparable punishment for twisting words.
rows.anchor: وعبر عنهم بالمؤتفكات لأن القصص للمنافقين الذين مبنى أمرهم على الكذب وصرف الأمور عن ظواهرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of afk in every arrangement centers on inversion: requiting turns an act back on its doer, and a lie turns speech away from its truth.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( إفك ) بكل ترتيب تدور على القلب , فإذا كافأت الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the hypocrites' mutual allegiance and threatening those like them with destruction for persisting without reflection, he turns to believers to invite repentance through hope in their state.
rows.anchor: عطف ببيان حال المؤمنين ترغبيا في التوبة طعما في مثل حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the hypocrites' 'some of them are of others,' the believers are allies without imitation or caprice: each follows the Messenger by conclusive proof, according to individual understanding, showing sound and rooted faith.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل : من , كما قال في المنافقين : من { بعض } دلالة على أن أحدا منهم لم يقلد أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their alliance means they stand together against outsiders like one body, whose other members respond with fever and wakefulness when one organ suffers.
rows.anchor: كالجسد الواحد إذا اشتكى منه عضو تداعى له سائر الجسد بالحمى والسهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿrūf is everything recognized and permitted by the revealed law.
rows.anchor: وهو كل ما عرفه الشرع وأجازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They likewise forbid wrong, showing no favoritism to anyone.
rows.anchor: { وينهون } أي كذلك { عن المنكر } لا يحابون أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They perform prayer with all its pillars, conditions, and limits, mindful of their Lord and drawing aid from it for whatever befalls them.
rows.anchor: يوجدونها على صفة تقتضي قيامها بجميع أركانها وشروطها وحدودها مراقبة لربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat is support for their poor, joining service to fellow creatures to service of the Creator; it contrasts with the hypocrites' withholding hands (9:67).
rows.anchor: مواساة منهم لفقرائهم صلة للخلائق بعد خدمة الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their obedience to God and His Messenger signals their good conduct and gracious companionship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى حسن سيرتهم وجميل عشرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised mercy parallels the hypocrites' being forgotten after forgetting God (9:67).
rows.anchor: وهذا مع الجملة قبله مواز لقوله في المنافقين { نسوا الله فنسيهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The road is rough and difficult, so the traveler depends on God's mercy, which is gracious treatment after forgiveness; no one can cross or arrive without it.
rows.anchor: فالسائر مضطر إلى الرحمة , وهي المعاملة بعد الغفران بالإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's invincible power lets Him aid His party and grant mercy without anyone preventing it; His wisdom makes His decree impossible to undo.
rows.anchor: فهو قادر على نصر من يوالي حزبه وأن ينيله من ثمرات الرحمة ما يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers remain victorious over every corrupter while they preserve mutual loyalty and its accompanying virtues.
rows.anchor: أن المؤمنين لا يزالون منصوورين على كل مفسد ما داموا على هذه الخلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding verse says God enriched them from His bounty, this pledge demonstrates both their withholding hands and their audacity in lying (9:74).
rows.anchor: ولما اقام سبحانه الدليل على ما ذكر بهذه الآية التي ختمها بانه أغناهم من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledger admits that any benefit comes from God's bounty, by any means—trade, booty, agriculture, or otherwise—and that no one has a claim on God.
rows.anchor: { لئن آتانا } أي من خير ما عنده , واعتراف بأنه لا حق لأحد عليه بقوله : { من فضله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic pledge reflects the liar's expectation that people will disbelieve him, as liars characteristically do.
rows.anchor: وأكد لأنه كاذب يظن أن الناس يكذبونه , وهكذا كل كاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to give from what God provides, without ostentation, as the assimilated pronunciation hints.
rows.anchor: من غير رياء - بما يشير إليه الإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim they will be thoroughly disposed to every good deed they are urged to perform.
rows.anchor: { ولنكونن } أي كونا هو الدال على أنا مجبولون على الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating 'from His bounty' confirms the pledger's own wording and stresses that God owes no one anything and no creature can cause or control His gifts.
rows.anchor: وكرر قوله : { من فضله } تقريرا لما قاله المعاهد تأكيدا للإعلام بأنه لا حق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They broke the emphatic pledge and withheld what was due, beyond merely failing to give voluntary secret charity.
rows.anchor: { بخلوا به } أي كذبوا فيما عاهدوا عليه وأكدوه غاية التأكد , فلم يتصدقوا بل منعوا الحق الواجب إظهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They forced themselves away from obeying the benefactor despite knowing the ugliness of breaking their pledge.
rows.anchor: { وتولوا } أي كلفوا أنفسهم الإعراض عن الطاعة لمن تفضل عليهم مع معرفتهم بقبح نقض العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away is in their hearts as well as their bodies; aversion was a settled trait already present when they made the pledge.
rows.anchor: { وهم معرضون * } اي بقلوبهم , والإعراض وصف لهم لازم لم يتجدد لهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān transmits al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report that the people were Nabtal ibn al-Ḥārith, Jad ibn Qays, Muʿattib ibn Qushayr, and Thaʿlaba ibn Khāṭib.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قال الضحاك : هم نبتل ابن الحارث وجد بن قيس ومعتب بن قشير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage escalates from ingratitude for a gift without a pledge to ingratitude after an explicit pledge, moving from the lesser offense to the greater.
rows.anchor: أن في الأولى كفران نعمة الغني من غير عهد , وفي هذه كفرانها مع العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse's grave requital highlights how serious it is to betray a covenant (9:77).
rows.anchor: ودل عظيم شأن العهد بتعظيم الجزاء على خيانته بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made their persistent miserliness result in entrenched hypocrisy in their hearts as punishment.
rows.anchor: { فأعقبهم } أي الله والتمادي على البخل جزاء علىذلك { نفاقا } متمكنا { في قلوبهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their meeting God here means death, when the opportunity for return has irretrievably passed.
rows.anchor: { إلى يوم يلقونه } أي بالموت عند فوت الفوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment matches their deed: it is for breaking the promise they made to God.
rows.anchor: { ما وعدوه } لأن الجزاء من جنس العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because breaking a promise is so ugly and entails disregard for lying, they lied habitually alongside their broken pledges.
rows.anchor: { وبما كانوا يكذبون * } أي يجدون الكذب دائما مع الوعدد ومنفكا عنه , فقد استكملوا النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exhibit the full set of hypocritical traits: betrayal, broken promises, and lies in speech.
rows.anchor: فقد استكملوا النفاق : عاهدوا غدروا ووعدوا فأخلفوا وحدثوا فكذبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their apparent enrichment could mislead the ignorant into thinking God did not know their inward state; judgment of their hearts instead proves He knows every heart better than its owner.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك ادل دليل على أنه تعالى أعلم بما في كل قلب من صاحب ذلك القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their secret is what their breasts conceal.
rows.anchor: { يعلم سرهم } وهو ما أخفته صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their private talk is what they discuss among themselves; nothing of it is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: { ونجواهم } أي ما فاوض فيه بعضهم بعضا , لا يخفى عليه شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the all-knower of every unseen thing.
rows.anchor: { علام الغيوب * } أي كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing their hidden dealings and consequences, God cannot be deceived; they should fear the outcome and fulfill their covenant.
rows.anchor: فيخشوا عاقبته فيوفوا بعهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's giving despite knowing their betrayal establishes the proof against them.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الإعطاء مع علمه بالخيانة إقامة الحجة

rows.speaker: علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān reports that ʿAlī, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, and al-Ḥasan read the question with second-person plural 'a-lam taʿlamū,' addressing the believers as an admonitory report.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وقرأ علي وأبو عبد الرحمن والحسن { ألم تعلموا } بالتاء , وهو خطاب للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to address believers signals that this knowledge benefits only those prepared for faith.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الالتفات الإشارة إلى أن هذا العلم إنما ينفع من هيىء للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their ingratitude for bounty and refusal of an obligation, the hypocrites go further and disparage generous believers who give from love of God, even beyond what is required.
rows.anchor: حتى تعدوه إلى عيب الكرماء الباذلين بصفة حبهم لربهم ما لم يوجبه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although only some made the taunts, the verse's broad form attributes the vice to all of them as a shared trait; lamz is covert fault-finding.
rows.anchor: { الذين يلمزون } أي يعيبون في خفاء { المطوعين } أي الذين ليس عليهم واجب في أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The volunteers are believers firmly rooted in faith.
rows.anchor: { من المؤمنين } أي الراسخين في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also singles out the poor to stress their added merit and show that encouraging a little good matters as much as encouraging much.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما مضى شاملا للموسر والمعسر , نص على المعسر لزيادة فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their 'effort' is the limit of their capacity, which they strain themselves to reach.
rows.anchor: إلا جهدهم } أي طاقتهم التي اجهدوا وأنفسهم فيها حتى بلغوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the gentle, pure counterpart to the preceding harsh group: the party whose repentance has been completed and whom God regards with mercy.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر هذا القسم المارد الجافي , ثنى بمقابلة اللين الصافي , وهي الفرقة التي نجز المتاب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deliberately named their sins in repentance, with regret, cessation, and resolve, rather than resorting to false excuses; they are those who stayed behind.
rows.anchor: { اعترفوا بذنوبهم } أي كلفوا أنفسهم ذكرها توبة منهم ندما وإقلاعا وعزما ولم يفزعوا إلى المعاذير الكاذبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction in 'another' evokes intermixture on both sides, an elegant iḥtibāk: they mixed good with evil and evil with good, suggesting neither was predominant.
rows.anchor: فالإتيان بالواو في { آخر } يفهم أن المعنى : { خلطوا عملا صالحا } بسيئ { وآخر سيئا } بصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī calls this a subtle instance of iḥtibāk and says the wording suggests the two kinds of deed are balanced, with neither taking priority as the basis.
rows.anchor: فهو من ألطف شاهد لنوع الاحتباك , ولعل التعبير بما أفهم ذلك إشارة إلى تساوي العلمين

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Samura reports in Bukhari's tafsir that the Prophet saw half-beautiful, half-ugly men become wholly beautiful after entering a river; they were people who mixed good and evil, whom God pardoned.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك في أناس رآهم في المنام شطر منهم حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's 'perhaps' assures hope of their repentance, although no one is entitled to anything from Him and every kindness is grace.
rows.anchor: فإن { عسى } منه سبحانه وتعالى واجبه لأن هذا دأب الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their restored status is like that of ordinary believers, who are not infallible and, despite lapses, expect mercy when they return to vigilance.
rows.anchor: فكما ان أولئك معدودون في حزب الله مع هذا التقصير المرجو له العفو فكذلك هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is always characterized by accepting the one who turns back and, through favor and generosity, replacing an evil deed with a good one.
rows.anchor: { إن الله } أي ذا الجلال والإكرام { غفور رحيم * } أي لم يزل موصوفا بقبول المعرض إذا أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to take a portion of their wealth is a compassionate step after repentance and a pleasing offering that confirms acceptance.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من شأن الرضوان قبول القربان , أمره صلى الله عليه وسلم تطهيرا لهم وتطيبا لقلوبهم بقوله : { خذ } ورحمهم بالتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity purifies them of sins and serves as expiation.
rows.anchor: { تطهرهم } أي هي من ذنوبهم وتجري بهم مجرى الكفارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses the Prophet's role as increasing them through good deeds, with God hearing his supplication and knowing his reforming intent.
rows.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ṣalli means the Prophet's supplication and visible affection toward them; God hears his prayer and knows his sincerity.
rows.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's prayer calms their hearts after anxiety about sin's outcome and reassures them that acceptance comes with God's approval.
rows.anchor: بعد قلق الخوف من عاقبة الذنب لما يعملون من أن القبول لا يكون إلا ممن حصل له الرضى عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reassurance also rests on knowing that God hears the Prophet's supplication and knows his sincerity in seeking their reform.
rows.anchor: من أن الله سمع قولك إجابة لك ويعلم صدقك في صلاحهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Biqāʿī relates that the remorseful absentees tied themselves to mosque pillars; the Prophet waited for God's order to release them, then took one-third of their offered wealth as charity after this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وذلك ان هذا الصنف لما اشتد ندمهم على التخلف اوثقوا أنفسهم بسواري المسجد فسأل عنهم رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because giving wealth was painful and the preceding promise used 'perhaps,' less-firm believers might hesitate to repent and give; the next verse reassures them that God accepts repentance and charity.
rows.anchor: وكان إخراج المال شديدا على النفوس لا سيما في ذلك الزمان , كان ربما استوقف الشيطان من لم يرسخ قدمه في الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone accepts sincere repentance and offerings, and His forgiving reception is an enduring attribute.
rows.anchor: التوبة } تجاوزا { عن عباده } اي التائبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reproaches the other absentees for failing to imitate the repentant group by showing remorse, binding themselves, and offering some wealth or a comparable sign of contrition.
rows.anchor: وفي ذلك إنكار على غيرهم من المختلفين في كونهم لم يفعلوا مثل فعلهم من الندم الحامل على أن يعذبوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Hūd gave advice with utmost clarity and showed signs that would ordinarily convince people, the only answer was rejection.
rows.anchor: جوابهم إلا أن { قالوا } اي عاد بعد أن أظهر لهم هود عليه السلام منا لمعجزات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him by his bare name instead of an honorific expresses harshness and rudeness.
rows.anchor: { يهود } نادوه باسمه غلظة وجفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial shows obstinate resistance to clear reason and transmitted proof, like the Arabs' demand for a sign despite the Prophet's innumerable signs (13:7).
rows.anchor: { ما جئتنا ببينة } فأوضحوا لكل ذي لب أنهم مكابرون لقويم العقل وصريح النقل

words: مَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they will neither move beyond nor turn away from their idols because of Hūd's statement.
rows.anchor: { وما نحن } وأغرقوا في النفي فقالوا : { بتاركي آلهتنا } مجاوزين لها أو صادرين { عن قولك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī notes their use of waw instead of causal fa, which would make the first statement the cause of the second.
rows.anchor: وتركهم للعطف بالفاء - المؤذنة بأن الأول سبب الثاني اي الواو في قولهم : { وما نحن لك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic negation and nominal sentence portray settled defiance; they refuse to follow Hūd out of obstinacy rather than sincere belief that he lacked a proof.
rows.anchor: دليل على أنهم تركوا إتباعه عنادا , لا أنهم يعتقدون أنه لم يأت ببينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyina is a clear proof that distinguishes truth from falsehood; bayān separates a meaning from others until it is clarified to the mind.
rows.anchor: والبينة : الحجة الواضحة في الفصل بينا لحق والباطل , والبيان : فصل المعنى من غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People reject manifest proofs by suppressing doubt, imitating leaders, accusing the source, adopting corrupt premises, or acting from envy; all these causes share the presence of doubt.
rows.anchor: مما سواه , والحامل على ترك البينة بعد ظهورها صد الشبهة عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī frames an implied question: if Hūd's statement seemed unclear or unjust, what motive would make him oppose his own cousins and closest people?
rows.anchor: ما ظهر لكم صحته فما تقولون إنه حملني عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied question sharpens the puzzle because Hūd's opposition risked alienating his cousins and dearest companions.
rows.anchor: فما تقولون إنه حملني عليه مع أن فيه منابذتكم وأنتم أولاد عمي وأعز الناس علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtarāka means that something afflicted and enveloped him, sticking to him forcefully like a knot clinging to what contains it.
rows.anchor: فقالوا : { إن نقول إلا اعتراك } اي أصابك وغشيك غشيانا التصق بك التصاق العروة بما هي فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They accuse one of their gods of afflicting Hūd with madness or derangement, which they claim explains his prohibition of idol worship.
rows.anchor: { بعض آلهتنا بسوء } من نحو الجنون والخبال فذاك الحامل لك على النهي عن عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature fears someone thought to have harmed it and capable of further harm, avoiding words that would displease that person.
rows.anchor: الإنسان يخشى ممن مسه بسوء وهو يتوهم أنه قادر على ضرره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their startling accusation draws the listener's attention to Hūd's answer.
rows.anchor: وكان قولهم محركا للسامع إلى الاستعلام عن حوابه لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd rejects their charge and shows that their gods are nothing, placing the idols with them among the powerless.
rows.anchor: { قال } نافيا لما قالوا مبينا أن آلهتهم لا شيء ضاما لهم معها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls God, the supreme sovereign, as witness to establish his innocence before Him.
rows.anchor: { إني أشهد الله } أي الملك الأعظم ليقوم عذري عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Out of deference, Hūd does not phrase his words as if equating the people with God; he commands them to witness so their incapacity is exposed and the proof stands against them.
rows.anchor: وعدل أدبا مع الله عن أن يقول : وأشهدكم - لئلا يتوهم تسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to witness publicly shows that Hūd considers the people and their religion negligible and expects everyone to recognize it.
rows.anchor: واشهدوا } أي أنتم لتقويم الحجة عليكم لأيكم ويبين عجزكم ويعرف كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He disavows the beings they associate with God and stresses their lowliness by saying they are apart from Him, whatever or whoever they are.
rows.anchor: { أني بريء مما تشركون * } وبين سفولها بقوله : { من دونه } كائنا ما كان ومن كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd challenges them to plot against him all together, individually if they choose, or collectively with their idols.
rows.anchor: { فكيدوني } حال كونكم { جميعا } أي فرادى إن شئتم أو مجتمعين أنتم وآلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because an immediate attack is more alarming and difficult, the particle thumma intensifies the challenge to give him no respite.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت المعاجلة في الحرب أهول , وكان شأنها أصعب وأخطر , بين عظمها بأداة التراخي فقال : { ثم لا تنظرون * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd is a covert scheme intended to provoke or inflict vexation.
rows.anchor: والكيد : طلب الغيظ بالسر في مكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This fearless challenge is a clear sign of Hūd's prophethood.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية من أعلام النبوة الواضحة لهود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied challenge is that Hūd is alone against their numbers and strength; he answers that he relies on God.
rows.anchor: فما حملك على الاجتراء على مخالفتنا نحن وأنت كثرتنا وقوتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawakkul means relying on God, the feared sovereign, who alone is king and Lord.
rows.anchor: { إني } أي جسرت على ذلك لأني { توكلت } معتمدا { على الله } الملك المرهوب عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Lord of both because He created them and directed their affairs before their creation, knowing what each would do for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { ربي وربكم } أي الذي أوجدنا ودبر أمورنا قبل أن يخلقنا فعلم ما بعمل كل منا في حق الآخرة

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has power and mastery over every creature, small or large, by taking it in a grip of force and conquest.
rows.anchor: { ما من دابة } أس صغرت أو كبرت { إلا هو آخذ } أي أخذ قهر وغلبة { بناصيتها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head; being seized by it means submitting to God's control and being unable to turn aside.
rows.anchor: ومن أخذ بناصيته فقد انقاد لأخذه لا يستطيع ميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word nāṣiya is connected etymologically with joining, as in two contiguous deserts described as tanāṣā.
rows.anchor: والناصية : مقدم الشعر من الرأس , وأصلها الاتصال من قولهم : مفازة تناصي مفازة - إذا كانت متصلة بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī explains inna causally here: because his Lord, who has sustained him, is upon a broad and clear road.
rows.anchor: { إن } أي لأن { ربي } أي المحسن إلي بما أقامني فيه { على الصراط } أي طريق واسع بين { مستقيم * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is manifest, broad, and free of ambiguity, defect, disorder, or deviation.
rows.anchor: ظاهر أمره لكل أحد لا لبس فيه أصلا ولا خلل ولا اضطراب ولا اعوجاج بوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beings worship, call upon, fear, and hope in God, even when some associate partners; only the worshippers honor idols, while others disregard them.
rows.anchor: فلذلك كان كل من في الكون يتألهه ويدعو ويخافه ويرجوه وإن اتخذ بعضهم من دونه شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the path is clear, its adherents know their purpose and remain firm, feared, followed, and loved; those who reject it go astray, and those who turn away are seized.
rows.anchor: فمن كان عليه كان علي القدر شهير الأمر , بصيرا بما يريد , مع الثبات والتمكن , مرهوب العاقبة

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since every forelock is in God's hand, He can protect those who rely on Him while their gods are powerless; He is Lord of idols, worshippers, and all things.
rows.anchor: فظهرت قدرته على عصمة من يتوكل عليه وعجز معبوداتهم معهمن لأن نواصي الكل بيده وهو ربها وربهم ورب كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending answers their claim that Hūd brought no proof: nothing is clearer than the affair of one whose Lord is on a straight path (11:53).
rows.anchor: فقد انطبقختام الآية على قولهم { ما جئتنا ببينة } ردا له لأن من كان على صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close also fits Hūd's answer about reliance and God's comprehensive control.
rows.anchor: وعلى جوابه في توكله وما في حيزه أتك انطباق
